bindings.label: Patient had shortness of breath for 1 month, which worsened over the past 2 days
Patient was a 32-year-old adequately nourished male, worked as a tailor, consumed a mixed diet, had BMI 25.3 kg/m2, and was well-built and nourished; he had no other accompanying symptoms

On examination, he was tachypneic, tachycardic, and had a mild fever; oral thrush was observed and scrapings were sent for fungal culture; SpO2 was 87%; no apparent risk factors for immunosuppressive states were found

Chest X-ray showed scattered inspiratory crackles; chest roentgenogram showed bilateral perihilar infiltrates; blood gas analysis revealed PO2 47 mmHg and PCO2 24 mmHg; HRCT thorax showed ground glass opacities in both lung fields, predominantly perihilar; LDH was elevated at 916 U/L; other routine blood work was normal

High flow oxygen was initiated and he was transferred to the Intensive Care Unit; he remained tachypneic on high flow oxygen and intermittently required noninvasive ventilation; empirical antibiotics, fluconazole, and oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMX) were started along with steroids

Bronchoalveolar lavage revealed Pneumocystis organisms; acid-fast bacteria and routine bacterial and fungal cultures were negative; fungal scrapings grew Candida albicans sensitive to fluconazole; HIV ELISA, Western blot, and HIV-RNA polymerase chain reaction tests were negative

Bacterial pneumonia
